pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: P1 - GPU autoscaler failing to scale (policy error + provider 429s). Triggered by 6141592653

sre-oncall (Maya): ack-ing, jumping in. seeing queue growth on eu-west pools, ~12m spike in queued requests.

infra (Raj): checked autoscaler logs, seeing repeated 'scale request rejected: rate_limit' from provider for vpool-eu-west-2. backoff is ramping.

eng-runtime (Lena): heap of queued KV cache ops and a long tail of small requests causing continuous new pods to be requested. autoscaler tried to scale but provider 429s caused controller to stop issuing new nodes.

Maya: impact? customers?

Lena: routing shows ~40% of production tenants in eu-west are getting 429 throttles and increased latencies (p95 from 120ms -> 2.1s). embeddings workloads worst.

cs (Ana): flagging 3 paying enterprise customers on EU region. one spinner just pinged support. I'll prepare a quick customer note.

Derek: assign roles: @infra handle provider side / tmp capacity, @eng-runtime handle fallback model routing and canary, @sre-oncall coordinate mitigations and pager.

Maya: mitigation plan (short):
- reduce per-tenant concurrency by 30% for eu-west (soft throttle)
- enable fallback to dedicated warm pool in us-east for critical customers
- temporarily drop small-batch-heavy tenants to a lower-CPU model variant to reduce scale requests

Raj: contacting provider support now, sending request id list and backoff traces. also trying to open an emergency quota exception. ETA unknown.

Lena: putting quick runtime change: add a transient routing rule that prefers warm pools for tenants with >10s queue growth. rolling out in 2m. snippet below:
```
- route: eu-west-heavy -> warm-pool-us-east
- policy: prefer-warm if queued > 50 requests OR avg wait > 3s
```

Maya: executing soft throttle: updating gateway limiters to 70% of prior concurrency for eu-west. will monitor queue length.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status changed to "Mitigating" by sre-oncall (Maya) at 6141592660

Raj: provider acknowledged, said they're experiencing internal control plane rate-limits and are lifting at 5-10 minute cadence. asked for our highest priority request to be moved to expedited queue.

Lena: after routing change, a subset of traffic started draining to warm pool. queue length down from ~22k -> ~4k in 6m. latency improving.

Ana: sent a targeted message to affected customer cohort (enterprise) explaining transient throttling and that we are routing to warm capacity. asked them to contact CS if they see continued failures.

Maya: monitoring metrics: token throughput normalizing, error rate dropped from 8% -> 1.5%, but autoscaler still showing scale_request_rejected counters intermittently.

Derek: good. next - do we need to spin additional reserved warm pool capacity in EU while provider recovers? cost/ops tradeoff?

Raj: we can launch a small reserved pool (4x 8xA100-equivalent) in eu-west via alternate provider partner, takes ~12m. request approval?

Maya: do it. prioritize tenancy that saw errors. I'll coordinate traffic shift. mark as emergency reserve.

Lena: adding an immediate safety in runtime to avoid generating new scale requests for very small loads: batching window extended from 5ms -> 30ms for eu-west for next 30m. expected to reduce scale churn.

pagerduty-bot: User note: on-call updated incident status to "Actionable mitigations applied" at 6141592674

Maya: short postmortem notes so far:
- Trigger: sudden provider control-plane rate-limits (429) combined with a workload pattern that generated many small, bursty scale requests.
- Failure modes: autoscaler backoff + repeated 429s prevented new capacity creation -> queue growth -> gateway throttles -> customer 429s/latency spikes.
- Immediate mitigations: soft concurrency throttles, route to warm pools, extended batching window, launch emergency reserved pool via partner.

Derek: action items (owners):
- infra (Raj): follow up with provider for RCA + request SLA credits; verify backoff behavior of autoscaler code path (due EOD).
- eng-runtime (Lena): add longer-term guard to debounce scale requests for small-batch tenants; implement dynamic batching knobs (due in 3 sprints).
- sre-oncall (Maya): write incident summary and draft customer-facing postmortem for CS review (due next business day).
- ops (Derek): evaluate a permanent small warm-buffer for EU to smooth short spikes (cost estimate in 2 days).

Ana: will send consolidated status update to affected accounts and include mitigation timeline.

Maya: closing notes: incident marked mitigated, continuing to monitor for 30m. prepare for full postmortem once provider responds with RCA. thanks team. :pray:

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved by sre-oncall (Maya) at 6141592680
